en: A ratio of the speed (of an object, etc.) to the speed of sound in the fluid or other medium through which the object travels. Usually us…

* Less commonly, a respelling of Hungarian Mács, a pet form of names corresponding to Matthew.

ex.ja: あのマヨネーズの中、添加物ばっかり！

ex.en: Mayonnaise and sesame paste go really well together.
ex.ja: マヨネーズと胡麻ペーストの相性は抜群だ。

ex.en: I have to buy mayonnaise and soy sauce.
ex.ja: マヨネーズと醤油を買わなきゃ。

note.ja: フランス語 mayonnaise から。スペインのメノルカ島の港町マオン（Mahón）にちなむとされる。

en: Of, relating to, or having melody.
Melodious, tuneful.

melodic.ety: Borrowed from French mélodique. By surface analysis, melody + -ic.

note.ja: melody + -ic。ギリシャ語 melōidia（歌）。「旋律の美しい」。

en: Characterized by very precise, conscientious attention to details.

meticulous.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin meticulōsus (“full of fear, timid, fearful, terrible, frightful”), from metus (“fear”) and -culōsus, extracted from perīculōsus (“perilous”). Sense of “characterized by very precise, conscientious attention to details” is a semantic loan from French méticuleux.

ex.en: It is not necessary to be meticulous.
ex.ja: こせこせする必要はない。

ex.en: He's not a very meticulous guy.
ex.ja: あいつもアバウトな性格だよな。

note.ja: ラテン語 meticulosus（びくびくした）から。metus（恐れ）。「失敗を恐れて慎重な」→「几帳面な」。

en: The quality of being modest; having a limited and not overly high opinion of oneself and one's abilities.
Moderate behaviour; reserve.

modesty.ety: Borrowed from Middle French modestie, from Latin modestia; equivalent to modest + -y.

ex.en: This is no time for modesty.
ex.ja: 謙遜している場合じゃないよ。

ex.en: Modesty is befitting to a young girl.
ex.ja: 若い娘には慎みが似つかわしい。

ex.en: Even when one is being praised, modesty is important.
ex.ja: 褒められても謙虚さが大事。

note.ja: modest（控えめな）+ -y。「謙虚さ」。

en: A growth of facial hair between the nose and the upper lip.
A curly bracket, { or }.

moustache.ety: Used in English since the 16th century. From Middle French moustache from Italian mostaccio, from Early Medieval Latin mustācium, from Medieval Greek μουστάκιον (moustákion), diminutive of (Doric) Ancient Greek μύσταξ (mústax, “upper lip”), of unknown origin (probably a Pre-Greek substrate). Replaced native English kemp (“moustache”), from Old English cenep.

ex.en: Tom grew a moustache.
ex.ja: トムは口ひげを生やした。

ex.en: "Hrmm," mumbled Professor Takeda as he twisted his moustache.
ex.ja: 「ふむ」 武田先生は口ひげを捻りながらうなった。

note.ja: mustache のイギリスのつづり。ギリシャ語 mystax（上唇）から。

en: Of a person, creature, group, or species, primarily active during the night.
Of an occurrence, taking place at night, nightly.
A person or creature that is active at night.
A device for telling the time at night, rather like a sundial but read according to the stars.

nocturnal.ety: From Middle French nocturnal, from Late Latin nocturnālis (“nocturnal”), from Latin nocturnus (“nocturnal”), from Latin nox (“night”), from Proto-Indo-European *nókʷts (“night”). Cognates include Ancient Greek νύξ (núx), Sanskrit नक्ति (nákti), Old English niht (English night) and Proto-Slavic *noťь.

ex.en: Some animals are nocturnal.
ex.ja: 夜に活動する動物もいる。

note.ja: ラテン語 nocturnus（夜の）から。nox（夜）。「夜行性の」。night と同じ祖先。

en: A short tube, usually tapering, forming the vent of a hose or pipe.
A short outlet or inlet pipe projecting from the end or side of a hollow vessel, as a steam-engine cylinder or a steam boiler.

nozzle.ety:
From Middle English noselle, equivalent to nose + -le (diminutive suffix).
Compare typologically Russian сопло (soplo) (<~ сопе́ть (sopétʹ), whence also сопа́тка (sopátka)).

note.ja: nose（鼻）+ -le。「小さな鼻」→「ノズル」。

en: In an illegal position ahead of the ball, puck, etc.
To the side of the road, past the curb and sidewalk.
An offside play.
The side of a road vehicle furthest from the kerb: the right side if one drives on the left of the road.

offside.ety: From off- + side. Compare German Abseite (“remote area, backside”), German abseits (“out of the way, apart, aside”, adverb), Dutch afzijdig (“neutral, impartial”).

ex.en: An offside... No! We did it!
ex.ja: オフサイド・・・じゃない！やったー！

note.ja: off（離れた）+ side（側）。「オフサイド」。

en: A secret rite or ceremony, typically involving riotous and dissolute behavior, including dancing, drunkenness and indiscriminate sexual a…
A gathering of people to engage in group sex.

orgy.ety: Originally in plural from French orgies, from Latin orgia, from Ancient Greek ὄργια (órgia, “secret rites, mysteries”).

ex.en: During the orgy Megumi ran naked round the lawn.
ex.ja: 乱交パーティーの中で、めぐみはすっぱだかで芝生を走り回った。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 orgia（秘儀）から。酒神の秘密の祭り →「ばか騒ぎ」。

en: To lay, spread, or apply (something) over or across (something else); to overspread.
To overwhelm; to press excessively upon.
An image to be overlaid on another; a superimposition or diapositive.
A piece of paper pasted upon the tympan sheet to improve the impression by making it stronger at a particular place.

overlay.ety: From Middle English overleyen, from Old English oferleċġan, from Proto-West Germanic *obarlaggjan, from Proto-Germanic *uberlagjaną, equivalent to over- + lay. Cognate with Saterland Frisian uurläze, úurlääse, Dutch overleggen, German Low German overleggen, överleggen, German überlegen, Swedish överlägga, Norwegian overlegge. Compare overlie.

note.ja: over（上に）+ lay（置く）。「重ねたもの」。

ja: 父親であること（paternity leave：父親の育児休暇）

en: Fatherhood, the state or quality of being a father.
Parental descent from a father.

paternity.ety: From Middle French paternité, from Old French, from Latin paternitās (“paternity”), from paternus (“of or pertaining to a father, paternal”) + -itās, from pater (“father”).

note.ja: ラテン語 paternitas（父であること）から。pater（父）。paternity leave（父親の育児休暇）。paternal と同じ。

en: Characteristic of a patriarch; venerable.
Relating to a system run by males, rather than females; relating to a patriarchy.

patriarchal.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin patriarchālis, from patriarcha + -ālis. Sychronically analyzable as patriarch + -al.

ex.en: Tom believes in a patriarchal society.
ex.ja: トムは男尊女卑思想の持ち主だ。

note.ja: patriarch（家長）+ -al。ギリシャ語 patēr（父）+ arkhein（支配する）。「家父長制の」。

en: So appalling or sad that one feels or should feel sorry for it; eliciting pity.
Eliciting contempt.

pitiful.ety: From Middle English pityful, piteful, piteeful. By surface analysis, pit(i) + -ful.

ex.en: The pitiful sight moved us to tears.
ex.ja: 気の毒な光景は私たちの涙をさそった。

ex.en: He's unlucky to a pitiful extent.
ex.ja: 彼は気の毒な程不運だ。

ex.en: The pitiful tale fetched tears from the girl.
ex.ja: その哀れな話を聞いて少女は涙を浮かべた。

note.ja: pity（哀れみ）+ -ful。「哀れな」。

en: An excessive amount or number; an abundance.
Excess of blood in the skin, especially in the face and especially chronically.

plethora.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin plēthōra, from Ancient Greek πληθώρα (plēthṓra, “fullness, satiety”), from πλήθω (plḗthō, “to be full”) + -η (-ē, nominal suffix).

ex.en: There is a plethora of adverbs of frequency in my language.
ex.ja: 私の言語は頻度を表す副詞の種類が豊富です。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 plēthōrē（満ちあふれること）から。「過多」。plenty と同じ祖先。

en: The transuranic chemical element with atomic number 94 and symbol Pu: a silvery-gray fissile radioactive actinide metal that tarnishes wh…
An atom of this element.

plutonium.ety:
Etymology tree
Ancient Greek πλοῦτος (ploûtos)
Proto-Indo-European *-Hō
Ancient Greek -ων (-ōn)
Ancient Greek Πλούτων (Ploútōn)bor.
Latin Plūtōbor.
Middle English Pluto
English Pluto
English -n-
Proto-Indo-European *-(i)yós
Proto-Italic *-ijos
Proto-Italic *-ios
Old Latin -ios
Latin -iusnom.
Latin -iumlbor.
English -ium
English plutonium
After Pluto (dwarf planet) + -n- + -ium. More in Wikipedia at plutonium § History.

note.ja: 冥王星（Pluto）にちなむ元素。uranium（天王星）、neptunium（海王星）に続く。

en: Required as a prior condition of something else; necessary or indispensable.
Something that is required as necessary or indispensable, or as a prior condition of something else.
A course or topic that must be completed before another course or topic can be started.

prerequisite.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *per-
Proto-Indo-European *preh₂-
Proto-Indo-European *-i
Proto-Indo-European *préh₂i?
Proto-Italic *prai
Proto-Italic *prai-
Latin prae-lbor.
Middle English pre-
English pre-
English requisite
English prerequisite
From pre- + requisite.

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ requisite（必要なもの）。「前提条件」。require と同じ。

en: A severe mental disorder, sometimes with physical damage to the brain, marked by a deranged personality and a distorted view of reality.

psychosis.ety: From psych- + -osis. Not descended from Ancient Greek ψύχωσις (psúkhōsis, “animation, principle of life”), which is a piecewise cognate.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 psychē（心）+ -osis（病的状態）。「精神病」。

en: To assign a quantity to.
To determine the value of (a variable or expression).

quantify.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *kʷ-
Proto-Indo-European *kʷos?
Proto-Indo-European *-onts?
Proto-Indo-European *kʷoider.?
Proto-Italic *kʷāntos
Latin quantus
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der.
Proto-Italic *θakos
Proto-Italic *-fakos
Latin -ficus
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu.
Proto-Italic *-ājō
Proto-Italic *-āō
Latin -ō
Latin -ficō
Medieval Latin quantificōder.
English quantify
From Medieval Latin quantifico (introduced by Sir William Hamilton in logic).

note.ja: ラテン語 quantus（どれだけ）+ -ify。「数量化する」。quantity と同じ。

en: An infectious disease caused by species of Lyssavirus that causes acute encephalitis in warm-blooded animals and people, characterised by…

rabies.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin rabiēs (“rage, madness, fury”). Doublet of rage.

note.ja: ラテン語 rabies（狂暴）から。rabere（狂う）。rage と同じ語源。

en: A portion of some limited resource, especially food, allocated to a person, group or period.
To supply with a ration; to limit (someone) to a specific allowance of something.
To portion out (especially during a shortage of supply); to limit access to.

ration.ety: From French ration. Doublet of reason and ratio.

ex.en: The government rationed meat during the war.
ex.ja: 戦時中政府は肉を配給にした。

ex.en: We have used our ration of coal for the week.
ex.ja: 一週間分の石炭を使ってしまった。

ex.en: They bargained additional rations of bread and milk.
ex.ja: 彼らはパンと牛乳の追加配給を交渉で決めた。

note.ja: ラテン語 ratio（計算）から。計算して割り当てた量 →「配給（量）・配給する」。rate、ratio と同じ。

en: Narration, account, description, rendering.
To tell; narrate; to relate in detail.

recount.ety: From Old Northern French and Anglo-Norman recunter, variant of Old French reconter.

ex.en: He recounted his unusual experiences.
ex.ja: 彼は奇怪な体験を詳しく話した。

ex.en: Island folklore still recounts the story of the raft.
ex.ja: 島の民間伝承はいまだにそのいかだの話を伝えている。

note.ja: re（再び）+ count（数える・語る）。「詳しく話す・数え直す」。

en: Any quadrilateral having opposing sides parallel and four right angles.
Such a quadrilateral that is oblong (longer than it is wide): one that is not regular (equilateral), that is, any except a square.

rectangle.ety: Borrowed from Middle French, from Old French, from Medieval Latin or Late Latin rectangulum (“right angle”), from Latin rectus (“right”) + angulus (“an angle”).

ex.en: The opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel.
ex.ja: 長方形の対辺は平行である。

ex.en: We encounter similar difficulties when we substitute rectangles for triangles in this configuration.
ex.ja: この構成において、三角形の代わりに長方形を用いても類似の困難が生ずる。

note.ja: ラテン語 rectus（直角の）+ angulus（角）。「長方形」。rectangular と同じ。

en: Recurring; happening time after time.
Non-transient.

recurrent.ety: From Latin recurrens, present participle of recurrere. Morphologically recur + -ent.

note.ja: re（再び）+ cur（走る）+ rent。再び走ってくる →「繰り返し起こる・再発する」。

en: An additional helping of food or drink at reduced cost.
Refuelling, fuel to refill an empty fuel tank (of a vehicle or machine) or other fuel container.
To fill up once again.
To repeat a prescription.

refill.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
English fill
English refill
From re- (“again”) + fill (noun).

ex.en: This refill lasts half a year.
ex.ja: この替え芯は半年持つ。

note.ja: re（再び）+ fill（満たす）。「お代わり・詰め替え」。

en: In the manner of religion.
Passionately or diligently; faithfully; conscientiously.

religiously.ety:
Etymology tree
English religious
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English religiously
From religious + -ly.

note.ja: religious + -ly。「宗教的に」→ 信仰のように「きちんと欠かさず」。

en: To experience (something) again; to live over again.
To come back to life.

relive.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
Middle English lefe
English live
English relive
From re- + live.

note.ja: re + live。「追体験する」。

en: Essential, indispensable, required.
An indispensable item; a requirement.

requisite.ety: From Latin requīsītus, perfect passive participle of requīrō (“to require, seek, ask for”), from which English require.

note.ja: re（再び）+ quis（求める）+ ite。必要として求められる →「必要な（もの）・必須条件」。

en: In a responsible manner.

responsibly.ety:
Etymology tree
English responsible
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English responsibly
From responsible + -ly.

ex.en: Cell phones are convenient, but I want them to be used responsibly.
ex.ja: 携帯電話は便利ですが、ちゃんとマナーを守って使ってほしいです。

note.ja: responsible + -ly。「責任をもって」。

en: Having undergone resurrection.

ex.en: He was PK'ed, I resurrected him.
ex.ja: ＰＫされたの、蘇生しました。

note.ja: resurrect（復活させる）+ -ed。ラテン語 resurgere（再び起き上がる）。resurrection（キリストの復活）。

en: To wind (something) again.
To wind back, of something clocklike or recordlike, like a cassette, tape, film; especially to then replay or relive.
The act of rewinding.
A button or other mechanism for rewinding.

rewind.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
Middle English wynden
English wind
English rewind
From re- + wind.

note.ja: re（元へ）+ wind（巻く）。「巻き戻す」。

en: In accordance with what is right or just.
Rightly, correctly.

rightfully.ety: From Middle English ryghtefully, equivalent to rightful + -ly.

note.ja: rightful（正当な）+ -ly。「正当に」。

en: Hidden, isolated, remote.

ex.en: My uncle lived alone in a secluded house on the cape.
ex.ja: 叔父さんは、岬の一軒家に独りぼっちで住んでいた。

note.ja: seclude（隔離する）+ -ed。se（離して）+ claudere（閉じる）。「人里離れた」。close と同系。

en: To beguile or lure (someone) away from duty, accepted principles, or proper conduct; to lead astray.
To entice or induce (someone) to engage in a sexual relationship.

seduce.ety: Borrowed from Latin sēdūcō (“to lead apart or astray”), from sē- (“aside, away, astray”) + dūcō (“to lead”); see duct. Compare adduce, conduce, deduce, etc. and Middle English seduct.

ex.en: I tried in vain to seduce her.
ex.ja: 彼女を誘惑しようとしたがむだだった。

ex.en: He seduced her with false promises.
ex.ja: 彼はでたらめな約束をして彼女を誘惑した。

ex.en: This guy is quick in seducing women so you better beware.
ex.ja: あの男は手が早いから気をつけた方がいいよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 seducere（脇へ連れ出す）から。se（離れて）+ ducere（導く）。「誘惑する」。produce と同じ duc。

ja: 正体のはっきりしない

en: In shadow; darkened by shadows.
Dark, obscure.

shadowy.ety: From Middle English schadwy, schadowy, equivalent to shadow + -y.

ex.en: It's getting more and more shadowy, soon it will be twilight.
ex.ja: いよいよ薄暮、もうすぐ宵闇。

note.ja: shadow + -y。「影の多い」→「正体のはっきりしない」。

en: To avoid, especially persistently; ostracize.
To escape (a threatening evil, an unwelcome task etc).

shun.ety:
From Middle English schonen (“to decline to do, avoid, fear”), from Old English sċunian (“to shun, fear, avoid”), of uncertain origin, though probably ultimately connected to the Proto-Indo-European root *(s)kewH- (“to cover, conceal”) via Proto-Germanic *skunōną; see that entry for more discussion.
Compare hide, shy, and Sanskrit स्कुनाति (skunāti, “to cover”).

ex.en: He's completely shunned. I'm surprised he's still working here.
ex.ja: あんな四面楚歌の状態で、彼よく仕事してられるよな。

ex.en: Shun will take over my job while I'm away.
ex.ja: 私が不在の間は俊が私の仕事を引き継ぎます。

note.ja: 古英語 scunian（避ける）から。「避ける」。

en: An assistant to another person, especially to a superior or more important person.
In literature, theatre, etc., a good foil of the protagonist, a character who helps emphasize the traits of the main character.

sidekick.ety: From side + kick, which in the late 19th and early 20th century was a slang term for the front side pocket of a pair of trousers, known as the pocket safest from theft. Thus, by analogy, a "side-kick" was a person's closest companion.

note.ja: side（わき）+ kick（ポケット：スリの隠語）。わきポケットのようにいつもそばにいる →「相棒」。

en: Twisted at an angle.
Biased, distorted

note.ja: skew（ゆがめる）+ -ed。古フランス語 eschiver（避ける）。「ゆがんだ・偏った」。

ja: 不安の種（英国のつづり）

en: UK and Australia standard spelling of specter.

ex.en: A spectre is haunting Europe — the spectre of communism.
ex.ja: 一匹の妖怪がヨーロッパを徘徊している。共産主義という妖怪が。

note.ja: ラテン語 spectrum（姿・幻）から。specere（見る）。「幽霊」。spectrum、inspect と同じ spec。

en: Specifically, one that is uncastrated.
A male horse kept primarily as a stud.

stallion.ety: From Middle English stalion, from Middle French estalon (whence modern French étalon), of Germanic origin, akin to stall. Displaced native Old English henġest.

note.ja: 古フランス語 estalon から。stall（馬小屋）と同系。馬小屋で飼う種馬。

en: The husband of one's biological mother after her initial marriage to or relationship with one's biological father.
The husband of one's parent distinct from one's biological father or person with a similar relationship.

stepfather.ety:
From Middle English stepfader, from Old English stēopfæder, from Proto-Germanic *steupafadēr (“stepfather”), equivalent to step- + father.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Stäiffoar (“stepfather”), Dutch stiefvader (“stepfather”), German Low German Steevvader (“stepfather”), German Stiefvater (“stepfather”), Swedish styvfar (“stepfather”), Icelandic stjúpfaðir (“stepfather”).

ex.en: My stepfather treats me better than my real father did.
ex.ja: 継父は、実父より良くしてくれます。

note.ja: 古英語 stēop（親を失った）+ father。「継父」。stepmother、stepchild。

en: To kill someone by squeezing the throat so as to cut off the oxygen supply.
To choke, suffocate or throttle, whether the victim survives or not.
A trading strategy using options, constructed through taking equal positions in a put and a call with different strike prices, such that …

strangle.ety: From Middle English stranglen, from Old French estrangler, from Latin strangulō, strangulāre, from Ancient Greek στραγγαλόομαι (strangalóomai, “to be strangled”), from στραγγάλη (strangálē, “a halter”); compare στραγγός (strangós, “twisted”) and string. Displaced Middle English worien (“to strangle”) (> English worry).

ex.en: The postmortem showed that she had been strangled.
ex.ja: 死体解剖の結果、絞殺と判明しました。

ex.en: My job is strangling rats.
ex.ja: 私の仕事は鼠を絞め殺す事です。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 strangalē（首つり縄）から。「絞め殺す」。

en: produced by synthesis
produced by a synthesizer

note.ja: synthesize（合成する）+ -ed。synthesis と同じ。synthesizer。

en: A heavy woven cloth, often with decorative pictorial designs, normally hung on walls.
Anything with variegated or complex details.
To decorate with tapestry, or as if with a tapestry.

tapestry.ety: From Middle English tapestrie, from Old French tapisserie (“tapestry”), from Ancient Greek τάπης (tápēs), from an Iranian source.

note.ja: 古フランス語 tapisserie から。tapis（じゅうたん）。「つづれ織り」。

en: Quality, state or condition of being tender.
A tendency to express warm, compassionate feelings.

ex.en: Tenderness is an important element in a person's character.
ex.ja: やさしさは人の性格の中で重要な要素だ。

ex.en: She said with deepest tenderness, "Are you all right"?
ex.ja: 彼女はとても優しく、大丈夫ですかと聞いた。

ex.en: She said her prayers, her heart full of love and tenderness.
ex.ja: 彼女は、心に愛情と優しさを込めてお祈りをした。

note.ja: tender（柔らかい・優しい）+ -ness。ラテン語 tener（柔らかい）。「優しさ」。

en: A dog from a group of small, lively breeds, originally bred for the hunting of burrowing prey such as rats, rabbits, foxes, and even otte…
Someone displaying terrier-like qualities such as determined pursuit.

terrier.ety: Borrowed from Middle French, from Old French chien terrier (“terrier dog”), from chien (“dog”) + Old French terrier (“of earth”, adjective), from Medieval Latin terrarius (“of earth”), from Latin terra (“earth”).

ex.en: She entered her terrier in a dog show.
ex.ja: 彼女は自分のテリア犬を犬品評会に出した。

note.ja: ラテン語 terra（大地）から。獲物を追って地面の穴に入る犬 →「テリア」。

en: A canopy over a bed.
Something that overhangs something else; especially a canopy or sounding board over a pulpit.

tester.ety: From Middle English tester, from Old French testre, from Latin testura.

note.ja: test + -er。「試験者」→「試供品」。

en: Any of several perennial composite plants, especially of genera Cirsium, Carduus, Cynara, or Onopordum, having prickly leaves and showy f…
This plant seen as the national emblem of Scotland.

thistle.ety:
From Middle English thistel, from Old English þistel, from Proto-West Germanic *þistil, from Proto-Germanic *þistilaz. *þīh- from *teyg-, which is a variant of Proto-Indo-European *(s)teyg- (“to prick”); from this same Proto-Indo-European root comes English stick.
Cognates include Scots thrissel, German Distel, Dutch distel, and Old Norse and Icelandic þistill.

note.ja: 古英語 thistel から。「アザミ」。スコットランドの国花。

en: The fingernail on the thumb.
A rough sketch (e.g., the size of one's thumbnail).
To describe concisely.
To create a smaller representation of (a larger image).

thumbnail.ety:
From thumb + nail. Compare West Frisian tommeneil (“thumbnail”), Dutch duimnagel (“thumbnail”), German Daumennagel (“thumbnail”).
The phrase thumbnail sketch was first attested 1852. Verb sense attested 1930s.

ex.en: I had my thumbnail torn off.
ex.ja: 親指の爪をはがしてしまいました。

ex.en: My thumbnail ripped off.
ex.ja: 親指の爪をはがしてしまいました。

note.ja: thumb（親指）+ nail（爪）。「親指の爪」→ 爪ほどの小さな画像 →「サムネイル」。

en: The act of tickling.
An itchy feeling resembling the result of tickling.
To touch repeatedly or stroke delicately in a manner which typically causes laughter, pleasure and twitching.
To feel as if the body part in question is being tickled.
Insecurely, precariously, unstably.

tickle.ety:
From Middle English tiklen, tikelen, of uncertain origin. Perhaps from a frequentative form of Middle English tikken (“to touch lightly”), thus equivalent to tick + -le; or perhaps related to Old English tinclian (“to tickle”). Compare North Frisian tigele (“to tickle”) (Hallig dialect), and tiikle (“to tickle”) (Amrum dialect), German dialectal zicklen (“to excite; stir up”).
Alternatively, from a metathetic alteration of Middle English kitelen ("to tickle"; see kittle). Both are ultimately sound-symbolic.

ex.en: I was tickled by her breath against my hair.
ex.ja: 彼女の息が髪に当たってくすぐったかった。

ex.en: Oh stop, that tickles!
ex.ja: もぅ、止めてよ。くすぐったい！

ex.en: Tom was tickled pink.
ex.ja: トムは天にも昇る思いだった。

note.ja: 中英語 tikelen から。tick（軽く触れる）と同系。「くすぐる」。

A period of observation or surveillance at any hour.
To participate in a vigil.

ex.ja: 彼女は病気の子供を徹夜で看病した。

en: The simultaneous firing of a number of missiles or bullets; the projectiles so fired.
A burst or emission of many things at once.
To fire a volley of shots.
To hit the ball before it touches the ground.

volley.ety: From Middle French volée (“flight”), from Vulgar Latin volta, from Late Latin volatus.

ex.ja: トムは田舎暮らしに憧れてるんだ。

Laughable; ridiculous.

A postage stamp issued to commemorate, usually a person or event; also commonly applied to thematic (topical) stamp issues.

discern.ety: From Middle English discernen, from Old French discerner, from Latin discernere (“to separate, divide, distinguish, discern”), from dis- (“apart”) + cernere (“to distinguish”); see certain.

ex.en: I discerned the potential of great things in him.
ex.ja: 私はあの人が将来偉くなると見取った。

ex.en: It is hard to discern between true and false.
ex.ja: ホントかウソかを見抜くのは難しい。

ex.en: It is hard to discern between the true and the false.
ex.ja: 本物と偽物を見分けるのは困難だ。

note.ja: dis（離して）+ cern（ふるい分ける）。ふるい分けて見分ける →「見分ける・識別する」。

ja: ドミノ（domino effect：ドミノ効果）

en: A tile divided into two squares, each having 0 to 6 (or sometimes more) dots or pips (as in dice), used in the game of dominoes.
A country that is expected to react to events in a neighboring country, according to the domino effect.
To collapse in the manner of dominoes.
To cause to collapse in the manner of dominoes.

domino.ety: 1801, borrowed from French domino (1771), originally the term for a hooded garment, itself from Medieval Latin domino, oblique case of dominus (“lord, master”); compare Medieval Latin dominicale (“a kind of veil”). By surface analysis, di- + -omino.

note.ja: イタリア語 domino（仮面舞踏会の頭巾付き外套）から。黒地に白い点の牌がその外套に似ていたことから。

en: A reduction of a rating, as a financial or credit rating.
A downhill gradient on a road or railway.
To place lower in position.
To reduce in complexity, or remove unnecessary parts; to dumb down.

note.ja: down + grade（等級）。「格下げする」。upgrade の対。
